cards.explanation: The answer is watching Jesus closely. Verse 1 says those in attendance were watching Him closely. That's one Sabbath meal with every eye on the guest, friends. When a whole table is staring at one person, I think something is about to happen.

The answer is healing on the Sabbath. Jesus asks, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?” (Luke 14:3). He puts the question to the experts in the law and the Pharisees, and He puts it right out loud. A man with dropsy is right there before Him, so the question is not just a theory.

The answer is False. They don't answer. Verse 4 says, “But they remained silent.” Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees straight out, and nobody spoke. I think that's a silence you could hear a cookie crumb drop in.

The answer is heals. Verse 4 says Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way. Nobody answered His question, and Jesus healed the man anyway, friends. Healed is the word the verse uses.

The answer is True. Jesus asks, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?” (Luke 14:5). Notice the word immediately, friends. Nobody in His question waits for the Sabbath to end.

The answer is the place of honor. Jesus says, “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor…” (Luke 14:8). He noticed how the guests were picking their seats and told them a parable. The best seat in the house is the one He says to leave alone.

The answer is that someone more distinguished may be invited. Jesus says not to sit there “…in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.” (Luke 14:8). Then verse 9 says the host will come and tell you, “Give this man your seat.” That's the risk of grabbing the place of honor, friends.

The answer is last. Verse 9 says the host will tell you to give your seat away, and “…in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.” You started at the top and ended at the bottom, friends. That's quite a drop.

The answer is True. Verse 10 says that when you sit in the last place, your host may come and say, “Friend, move up to a better place.” That's the opposite of the humiliation in verse 9. This time the host is the one who tells you to move up.
The answer is honored. Verse 10 says, “Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.” The honor comes after the host moves you up, friends. And the whole table sees it.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.” (Luke 14:11). Exalting yourself leads to being humbled, friends. It's one line, and it flips the whole seating chart.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors.” (Luke 14:12). That's the guest list He says to skip. I'd love to have seen the host's face.

The answer is that they may invite him in return. Jesus says, “Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.” (Luke 14:12). If they invite you back, you've been repaid right there, friends. It's like trading dinners and calling it even.

The answer is True. Verse 13 says, “But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind…” Jesus flips the guest list from the people who can repay you to the people who can't. It's the same room, with a very different table.

The answer is at the resurrection of the righteous. Jesus says, “Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.” (Luke 14:14). Those are the guests He tells the host to invite, and they can't repay him. So the repaying comes at the resurrection of the righteous, friends.

The answer is that everyone who eats at the feast in God's kingdom is blessed. One of those reclining with Jesus says, “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.” (Luke 14:15). He hears Jesus talk about a banquet and the resurrection, and he answers with that. And Jesus has a story ready.

The answer is come because everything is ready. The servant tells those who had been invited, “Come, for everything is now ready.” (Luke 14:17). The invitation went out first, and now it's time, friends. Everything's done and the table is waiting.
The answer is False. Verse 18 says, “But one after another they all began to make excuses.” They'd been invited, and they didn't come, friends. One excuse after another.

The answer is that he is going to try them out. The man says, “I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.” (Luke 14:19). Five yoke is a lot of oxen to try out on banquet day, friends.

The answer is True. The third man says, “I have married a wife, so I cannot come.” (Luke 14:20). Notice he says cannot, not please excuse me like the other two. Three men, three reasons, and none of them show up.
The answer is angry. Verse 21 says, “Then the owner of the house became angry…” The servant reported all of it, and that's how the owner reacts, friends. Then he sends the servant out again.

The answer is the same people Jesus told the host to invite. The owner says to bring in “…the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.” (Luke 14:21). Earlier Jesus told the host to invite “…the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind…” (Luke 14:13). That's the same group Jesus named to the host, friends.

The answer is to the highways and hedges. The master says, “Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in…” (Luke 14:23). The servant already did the streets and alleys, and there's still room. So the search goes further out, friends.

The answer is full. The master says, “…so that my house will be full.” (Luke 14:23). The servant said there was still room, and the master wants none left. Think of a cookie jar he plans to see packed to the brim.

The answer is False. The master says, “For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.” (Luke 14:24). They were invited first and gave their excuses, friends. That's where Jesus ends the story.
